title: Count Uppercase Letters
description: Given a string s, return the number of uppercase English letters in it.

examples.explanation: H and W are uppercase letters.

hints: Loop through each character.
str.isupper() checks whether a character is uppercase.
reference_solution:
def solve(s):
    return sum(ch.isupper() for ch in s)

title: Rotate List Right
description: Given a list nums and a non-negative integer k, return a new list with the elements rotated k positions to the right.

examples.explanation: The last two elements move to the front.

hints: If the list is empty, return an empty list.
Use k % len(nums) so very large rotations wrap around.

title: Flatten One Level
description: Given a list containing values and lists, return a new list with each nested list expanded by exactly one level. Do not recursively flatten deeper lists.

examples.explanation: Each inner list is expanded once.

hints: Build a new result list.
Use isinstance(item, list) to decide whether to extend or append.

title: Chunk List
description: Given a list nums and a positive integer size, return a list of consecutive chunks, each containing at most size elements.

examples.explanation: The list is split into groups of two except for the final shorter group.

hints: Move through the list in steps of size.
nums[i:i + size] creates one chunk.
reference_solution:
def solve(nums, size):
    return [nums[i:i + size] for i in range(0, len(nums), size)]

title: First Repeated Character
description: Given a string s, return the first character that appears at least twice when scanning from left to right. Return an empty string if every character is unique.

examples.explanation: The second occurrence of a is the first repeated character encountered.

hints: Keep a set of characters already seen.
As soon as a character is already in the set, return it.

title: Group Words by Length
description: Given a list of words, return a dictionary mapping each word length to the list of words having that length, preserving their original order.

examples.explanation: Words are grouped by their character count.

hints: Use the word length as the dictionary key.
Append each word to the list stored for that key.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string containing only parentheses (), square brackets [], and curly braces {}, return True if every opening bracket is correctly closed in the proper order.

examples.explanation: Each opening bracket is closed in reverse order.

hints: Push opening brackets onto a stack.
For a closing bracket, the top of the stack must contain its matching opener.

title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
description: Given a list of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the resulting intervals sorted by their start value.

examples.explanation: The first two intervals overlap, and the last two intervals overlap.

hints: Sort intervals by their start value first.
If the next interval starts before or at the current end, extend the current interval.

title: Product Except Self
description: Given a list of integers nums, return a list where each position contains the product of every value in nums except the value at that position. Do not use division.

examples.explanation: Each result is the product of all elements except the one at the same index.

hints: First store the product of all elements to the left of each position.
Then multiply each position by the product of all elements to its right.
reference_solution:
def solve(nums):
    out = [1] * len(nums)
    prefix = 1
    for i, value in enumerate(nums):
        out[i] = prefix
        prefix *= value
    suffix = 1
    for i in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        out[i] *= suffix
        suffix *= nums[i]
    return out

title: Top K Frequent Values
description: Given a non-empty list of integers nums and an integer k, return the k values that occur most frequently. If frequencies tie, return the smaller value first.

examples.explanation: 1 occurs three times and 2 occurs twice.

constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, 1 <= k <= number of distinct values
hints: Count each value with a dictionary.
Sort the distinct values using frequency descending and value ascending.
